meaning: FS = 100.0 hard-codes the sampling rate assumed for the jugular recordings in data/4_exemples. Every time axis, filter design and window length built in this preparation script derives from that one number.

could_move.what: Filter cutoffs passed to butter/filtfilt are normalised by FS, so a wrong FS shifts the effective corner frequency and changes how much of the créneau edge survives smoothing.
The pre-window baseline is counted in samples against FS, so the level the model settles to may be read off a longer or shorter stretch than intended.
Everything written to data/jugular_prepared inherits the assumed time base, so any later fit to these targets is stretched in time by the same factor.

expectation: Direction unknown. If the true rate differs from 100 Hz by a factor k, prepared signals are time-scaled by k and fitted time constants move roughly with k. If the files really are 100 Hz, no effect. The reach trace found no references, so I cannot see which decks consume the output.

check.why: Prints the first raw example's columns, first rows and length so a human can compare any timestamp spacing against the assumed 100 Hz without re-running a fit.
